protections: P1: a media or file source string taken from an HTTP request body (image_url, audio_url, video_url, Anthropic url source, Responses input_image/input_file) must not name a server-local file (bare path or file://) and must not be fetched from a loopback, private, link-local or local-named host, judged on the resolved address and re-checked on every redirect. Trusted in-process callers (CLI interactive mode, library users) keep local-file access.

mistralrs-server-core/src/util.rs:59-64 (reqwest::get on any http/https host, default redirect policy, no host check)
mistralrs-server-core/src/util.rs:65-78 (file:// read of the whole file)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: An in-process Python library whose caller is trusted, the same as the fix's Local policy. The advisory is about the HTTP server.
evidence: mistralrs-pyo3/src/util.rs:202-248 (sync copy: bare path, file://, reqwest::blocking::get without host check)

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T1/T2/T3 (drop file:// and bare-path support from util::parse_image_url/parse_audio_url and video::parse_video_url) breaks the CLI interactive callers and the project test at util.rs:240-249. The fix has to be a server-only policy or variant, chosen at chat_completion.rs:931/940/949.

Copying the T4 literal-only reject_private_host into the media loaders looks like a consistent fix. It leaves DNS names, redirects and IPv6 literals open in both places, so fixing T1 by reusing T4 carries T4's weakness over.

fairness_risks: Server-local media paths: a self-hosting operator might legitimately send local paths to their own server. The fix refuses them for HTTP requests, which hidden tests should enforce only on the server path and never on util::parse_image_url's default (Local) behaviour (util.rs:240-249).
data: URLs must stay accepted on all server routes (util.rs:290-298; responses.rs:157; anthropic.rs:887).
Public http(s) media URLs must stay accepted. The existing test needs network to rust-lang.org (util.rs:232-238), so hidden tests must not depend on outbound fetches.

Redirect re-validation and DNS-resolves-to-private cases are hard to test offline: a local test HTTP server sits on 127.0.0.1, which the guard itself must reject. Hidden tests for those shapes need an injectable resolver or client, which a solver's design may not expose. Keep hidden tests to literal IPs (including bracketed IPv6 like [::1] and ::ffff:127.0.0.1), localhost names, bare paths and file:// URLs.
T7 (pyo3) matches the fix's own trusted Local policy, so a hidden test requiring it to reject local files would contradict upstream intent.

design.why: Four independent groups, each with a different reason to dismiss. T1 (with T2/T6 riding along) is the reported route. T3 is a second loader hidden in a frame-extraction module ('not a URL loader'). T4 is a neighbouring feature with an existing but weak guard ('already protected'); the bracketed-IPv6 host_str bug and the unchecked redirects are concrete and partly testable offline. That makes it the deepseek-type trap. T5 is the coupled must-keep-working local-file behaviour for CLI and the project test. That makes it the mimo-type trap, aimed at over-hardening. T7 is left out because the trusted-caller dismissal is upstream's own position, so a hidden test there would be unfair.
